solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Self-assured hipster regularly seen in school

indicators.note: seen in places the picked letters inside the word for a school

parts.note: a school of whales or dolphins is a pod

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of hipster, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A confident trendy young man is spotted at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a place of learning, but it is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone composed and calm in manner is self-assured.

clue.text: Some toreadors getting upset in a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the run of letters reads backwards
Some signals that only part of the word toreadors is used

explanation.surface: Bullfighters lose their tempers in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks OREA from inside toreadors and 'getting upset' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Aero is a well-known bubbly chocolate bar made by Nestlé in Britain.

clue.text: Might attempt to draw attention to wilful infliction of injury

parts.note: might, as a verb of possibility, can be may
a hem or ahem is a little cough made to catch someone's notice

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get noticed by deliberately hurting others.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: in old law the crime of maiming someone deliberately was called this, and more widely it means violent chaos.

clue.text: Put forward Weasley as possible contributor to annihilation

parts.note: to posit is to put forward an idea for consideration
Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's friend in the novels

explanation.surface: A Weasley from Harry Potter is proposed as a wizard who might help wipe out an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics: when this antiparticle meets an electron, the pair annihilate each other in a burst of energy.

clue.text: General whose anger carries some weight? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: carries would put the weight below the anger in this down light, and the exclamation 'Just the opposite!' turns that around so anger sits on top

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger
a ton is a weight of 2,240 pounds

explanation.surface: A general whose temper gives him clout, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' with 'Just the opposite!' means the weight carries the anger, so in this down entry anger comes first, above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical figure: Henry Ireton was a Parliamentarian general in the English Civil War and Cromwell's son-in-law.

clue.text: Arranged seminar on Sweden that doesn't quite hit the target

definitions.text: that doesn't quite hit the target

indicators.note: Arranged tells us the letters of seminar are put in a new order

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A seminar organised on Sweden that misses its aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges seminar; S for Sweden then sits after it, the 'on' being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a shot or attempt that comes close but fails to strike its aim is called this.

clue.text: The dawn chorus?

parts.note: birdsong heard at first light is music made at an early hour, whimsically read as a genre of old repertoire

explanation.surface: Birds singing at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: The genre name for medieval, Renaissance and Baroque repertoire is read literally as tunes played at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: the genre label for pre-1750 classical pieces literally describes songs performed at sunrise, like birdsong.

clue.text: Place not initially in Atlas it turned out

indicators.note: turned out signals that the gathered letters are rearranged into a new word
initially takes just the opening letter of not

explanation.surface: A place missing from an atlas, as it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives N; 'turned out' rearranges N with ATLAS and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend: Plato's sunken island is a mythical place never found on any real map.

clue.text: Herb Lear's middle daughter's concealed in middle of food

indicators.note: concealed in puts the daughter's name inside the letters picked from food
middle of takes the central letters of food, its two O's

parts.note: Regan is the second of King Lear's three daughters, between Goneril and Cordelia

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean daughter is sneaked into a dish as a seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' appears twice: once for the daughter's place in the family, once as the indicator taking the inner letters of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: marjoram's wild cousin is a culinary herb used widely in Italian and Greek cooking.

clue.text: What members of the Sealed Knot do: carry stick around in wet

definitions.text: What members of the Sealed Knot do

indicators.note: carry means the soaking word holds the turned stick inside it

parts.note: to ret flax or hemp is to soak it in water to soften the fibres

indicators.note: around tells us the stick word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: Civil War enthusiasts lug sticks about in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sealed Knot is a British society that stages English Civil War battles. Ret, to soak flax, is an uncommon word; 'around' reverses the stick and 'carry' holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the society's members stage historical battles again for the public, playing out past events.

clue.text: Keep quiet about biblical character's reluctance to work

indicators.note: about means the silencing letters go around the biblical name

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis, whose wife became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Hushing up the idleness of someone from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reluctance to work' defines a noun, and the deadly sin of idleness fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: laziness or idleness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Bury boxer with aggression primarily among other things

parts.note: to inter is to bury
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of aggression

explanation.surface: Laying a fighter to rest, along with his combative spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: the Latin phrase is used in English to mean including various other items.

clue.text: Remove the prime minister's books

parts.note: the prefix de- signals removal, as in de-bone or de-ice
David Cameron was the UK prime minister when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: An instruction to oust the PM, with his own library.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': DE plus CAMERON is the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature: Boccaccio's collection of a hundred tales is a work in ten parts, so a set of books.

clue.text: All Connie can cook without nuts at first: pasta

indicators.note: can cook says the following letters are cooked up into a new arrangement
at first takes only the opening letter of nuts

explanation.surface: Connie can make a pasta dish entirely without nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is a link here, not an instruction: N joins ALLCONNIE, and 'can cook' rearranges all ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: large tubes of pasta, usually stuffed and baked in sauce.

clue.text: One spot around front of mosque in Turkish city

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: around means the spot word goes outside the picked letter

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of mosque

explanation.surface: A sightseer picks out a place near a mosque in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: an industrial port city on the Sea of Marmara in north-west Turkey.

clue.text: Hold murderer without leg restraint at last

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the murderer goes round the rest

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of restraint

explanation.surface: Detaining a killer, with the leg shackle put on last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side; 'at last' takes the final letter of restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep something within limits is to hold it.

clue.text: Move all the fielders to the onside? Get lost!

definitions.text: Move all the fielders to the onside?
definitions.meaning: in cricket, emptying the off side of fielders would literally clear that half of the field
a rude instruction to go away

explanation.surface: A cricket captain rearranges his field, and someone is told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field splits into the off side and the on (leg) side; shifting every fielder over leaves one half empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a curt command telling someone to leave, read literally as emptying the off side.

clue.text: Dismay about remotely-operated vehicle gaining acceptance

indicators.note: about means the dismay word goes round the vehicle's letters

parts.note: to appal is to dismay
ROV is the standard abbreviation for a remotely operated vehicle, such as an underwater drone

explanation.surface: Alarm at an unmanned vehicle finding favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: approval and acceptance both mean a favourable reception.

clue.text: Demands to be among first on board

indicators.note: among says the ordinal is placed between the letters for being aboard

parts.note: on board is in SS, aboard a steamship
first is written 1st, read as the letters IST

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be one of the first to get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts IST (1st) inside IN SS (on a steamship); 'to be' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who demands something firmly will not back down on it.

clue.text: Caterpillar heading for Mundesley after Norwich is devastated

indicators.note: is devastated says the city's letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
heading for takes the opening letter of Mundesley

explanation.surface: A caterpillar crawls toward a Norfolk seaside village after Norwich is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Mundesley is a village on the Norfolk coast, near Norwich. 'is devastated' rearranges NORWICH plus M.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the looping larva of a geometer moth, which moves as if measuring the ground.

clue.text: Appraise an important person in 'ackney, say

indicators.note: Hackney is in east London, where Cockney speech drops the h, as the apostrophe shows

parts.note: a high-up is someone of high rank

explanation.surface: Sizing up a VIP in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, who drops the h, would say 'igh up; Hackney is an East London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrasal verb means to look someone over with interest, often appreciatively.

clue.text: Verse writer for Bad Co., ABC and 10CC

indicators.note: Bad says the letters are messed up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the digits 1 and 0 are read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A lyricist writing for three rock and pop bands: Bad Company, ABC and 10cc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad', which looks like part of the band name Bad Company, rearranges CO, ABC and IOCC.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature: the Italian writer of The Decameron also composed narrative poems, so he was a poet.

clue.text: Dance attire

definitions.meaning: a Spanish dance in triple time
a short open jacket, an item of clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lively Spanish dance, and a short jacket worn open at the front.

clue.text: Primate seemingly agreeable among sailors

definitions.meaning: a nocturnal lemur of Madagascar with a long thin middle finger
sailors reply to an order with '..., sir', so the phrase sounds like naval agreement

explanation.surface: An ape who seems to get on well with the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a Madagascan lemur, and the naval reply meaning yes, understood.

clue.text: Some perversely classed oloroso as port

indicators.note: perversely means the run of letters is read the wrong way round
Some signals that only a run of letters from classed oloroso is used

explanation.surface: Some people wrongly class a sherry as a port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ASSEDO from inside classed oloroso and 'perversely' turns it round. 'port' looks like the wine; here it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Nomocracy's awful role in revolution

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: nomocracy is government by a code of laws

indicators.note: in revolution says the letters are turned about and reordered

explanation.surface: A legal system plays a dreadful part during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'in revolution' rearranges AWFUL ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: government according to fixed laws rather than by a ruler's whim.

clue.text: Lofty home that may sound strange to some

indicators.note: may sound, to some speakers, tells us the word is said aloud like another

parts.note: eerie means strange and unsettling

explanation.surface: A high-up house that some people find weird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some' hedges because not every speaker says the two words the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an eagle's nest built on a crag is a high dwelling.

clue.text: Boy one associated with private saving account

definitions.text: one associated with private saving account
definitions.meaning: read as a bank account, this hides the film Saving Private ..., whose title character is the private being saved

explanation.surface: A lad linked to a personal savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: The banking surface hides a 1998 war film, Saving Private Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a boy's first name, and the soldier rescued in a Spielberg war film.

clue.text: Not just attending function in amusement park

indicators.note: attending means the fairness word accompanies the function letter, coming after it

parts.note: f is the mathematical abbreviation for a function
something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: Going to a party at a theme park is not entirely fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely' but means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a travelling show with rides and stalls is a fair for amusement.

clue.text: Shades of fish embargoes

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
embargoes are bans on trade

explanation.surface: Varieties of colour in fish trade restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand: a well-known make of sunglasses, which are informally called shades.
